answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before earning rewards, with slashing on proven fraud. One honest agent pays the bond once, like a single meadow plot tended by one keeper, while a farm spawning a thousand clones must lock a thousand bonds, so its cost scales linearly while its reward stays flat. The crystal-clear public ledger makes every bond and slash auditable, and reputation from verified work accrues only to the bonded key, never to a copied name. Each identity must sing the same sonnet of proof: stake, work, accountability.
